content.title: Air France-KLM reports solid third-quarter results despite rising costs
content.summary:
STORY: Air France-KLM reported solid third-quarter results Thursday (November 6) despite rising costs.

The airline also confirmed its outlook for this year even though it has seen higher expenses and costly challenges for KLM.

The group reported an operating profit of $1.40 billion - just below analyst forecasts but slightly higher than last year.

CEO Ben Smith said the carrier showed its resilience in a challenging environment during the period.

The group was particularly helped by lower fuel costs and solid bookings in its more luxurious premium cabins.

But it saw pressure on yields in its economy cabin with travel to the U.S.

European airlines have faced pressure as travel from Europe to the U.S. has dropped under President Donald Trump.

KLM was hit by lower yields in its economy cabin, as well as costly labor disputes in September. 

Air France-KLM shares were down 13% in early trade.

Investors were worried by the slight misalignment in expectations on the carrier's operating profit due to currency depreciation.

They also saw ongoing challenges with budget carrier Transavia and Dutch subsidiary KLM.
